Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
124 PM PST Thu Nov 19 2026

.SYNOPSIS...19/1230 PM.

Scattered showers are expected through the evening, then dry
weather will return Friday through Sunday afternoon with highs
around 5 degrees below normal. Overnight lows will be chilly as 
well with some areas dropping below freezing. Light rain is 
possible Sunday night into Monday and again next Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SUN)...19/104 PM.

A very potent storm moved through the area today dropping
extremely heavy rain. Peak rates topped out at 2.26" in one hour
over Mulholland Dr above Encino, which statistically was a once 
in 100 year event. Scattered showers are expected through this
evening but no further significant impacts are expected.

Friday through Sunday afternoon will be dry, though temperatures
will be on the cooler side, mainly in the 60s. Overnight lows will
be chilly, especially interior areas where some sub-freezing
temperatures are possible, most likely in the Antelope Valley and
parts of interior SLO County. Some light northeast winds are
expected this weekend as weak offshore flow develops. Winds likely
topping out in the 20-30 mph range.

A very weak system will move into the area Sunday night into
Monday morning. At most maybe a quarter inch of rain along the 
Central Coast and a tenth or less to the south.

.LONG TERM (MON-THU)...19/122 PM.

The rest of Monday and Tuesday will be dry with a slow warming
trend. 

Another weak system will move into the state Wednesday. Models are
mixed on whether we will get any rain from it. If so it probably 
won't be much, though there is a small portion of the ensembles
that show around a half inch of rain.

In any case, Thanksgiving is expected to be dry with some offshore
flow that will push temperatures into the 70s.

&&

.AVIATION...19/1823Z.

At 1736Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Moderate confidence in all TAFs. Through about 20Z cig/vis will 
vary frequently especially over L.A. County. MVFR/VFR conds will 
be most frequent but isolated IFR conds are likely as well in 
heavier showers. There is a 20% chance of thunderstorms through 
20/00Z for L.A. County.

KLAX...Low confidence in TAF. There will be frequent cig/vis
changes thru 19Z. There is a 20 percent chc of a TSTM thru 20/00Z.
No east wind component is expected during the fcst period.

KBUR...Moderate confidence in TAF. There will be frequent cig/vis
changes thru 20Z. There is a 20 percent chc of a TSTM thru 20/00Z.

&&

.MARINE...19/1226 PM.

High confidence in dangerous ocean conditions through tonight  
due to a combination of gusty winds and large seas. Seas will 
continue to increase due to the combination of a large northwest 
swell and southwest wind swell. Large breaking waves may impact 
Morro Bay Harbor and to a lesser extent Ventura Harbor through 
tonight.

Conditions will improve through the day Friday and become relatively
mild through Saturday. A weak front will likely move through the
coastal waters Sunday into Monday but impacts look minimal at
most. Looking ahead, another stronger cold front could impact the
coastal waters Tuesday night into Wednesday with wind and rain.
Large seas are also expected to return to the coastal waters
around mid to late next week.

&&

.BEACHES...19/1226 PM.

Large surf will create very dangerous rip currents and jetty 
conditions into Friday. High Surf Advisories remain in effect for
all beach areas.

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional swells are becoming increasingly likely next week as
well. These swells may produce period of elevated to high surf.

The combination of very high tides and increasing surf next week 
will likely lead to at least widespread moderate-level coastal 
flooding issues across all coasts. There is potential for 
significant coastal flooding impacts if a larger swell overlaps 
with the timing of the extreme tides
